fields.title: Value proposition is an answer, not a description
fields.keyTakeaway: A value proposition exists only in pairs: on the left is the customer's job, pain, and gain; on the right is what exactly you do for each of them. An item on the right with nothing to answer on the left is a feature without a reason.
fields.checkQuestion: The team proposes adding an executive dashboard. How do you verify that this is a value proposition and not just decoration?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **what value propositions solve customer jobs?**
fields.blocks/1/text: Domain end-to-end example: Dispetcher is a fictional internal product of the Surma transport company: 60 vehicles, long-haul trucking, route planning, and driver assignment. In block V1, we determined whose need this was and what counts as done. Here, we look at how a need becomes a solution.
fields.blocks/2/text: **What happens if you do not answer the question.** A list of features appears, where everyone likes a different feature. You can debate such a list endlessly: any feature will find a defender, and none has a verifiable reason.
fields.blocks/3/items/0: **Left side — customer profile:** jobs, pains, gains (we collected these in D2).
fields.blocks/3/items/1: **Right side — your solution:** what relieves pain (pain reliever), what creates gain (gain creator), which part of the product is responsible for it.
fields.blocks/3/items/2: **Fit** is not the whole picture, but the links between the sides: every element on the right is tied to an element on the left.
fields.blocks/3/items/3: **Test:** cover the left half. If the right half still sounds convincing, you described features, not value.
fields.blocks/4/text:
Feature: "Automatic assignment of drivers to routes."

Value proposition:
The dispatcher's pain — on Monday morning, they manually reconcile 60 vehicles and 74 drivers, spending two hours and assigning a driver without the required license category once a week on average.
What we do — offer assignments in seconds and prevent assigning a driver who lacks the required category.
Gain — Monday planning wraps up by 9:30 instead of 11:00, and there are no category errors.

The former can be discussed forever. The latter is tested two weeks after release.
fields.blocks/5/text: The left side usually collects fifteen items, while you only have enough capacity for three. They are picked using two criteria: how often the pain occurs and what a person does when it occurs. A pain that is bypassed with a single habit is almost never worth building for.
fields.blocks/5/title: Not every pain deserves an answer
fields.blocks/6/text: **The reverse direction is also useful.** Take what is already in the backlog and try to tie it to the left half. Usually, a third cannot be tied — that is the cheapest way to cut the plan.
fields.blocks/7/text: The canvas does not tell you how many people experience the pain or how much they will pay for it. It checks the coherence of the idea, not its size: unit economics are calculated separately in the "Economics" domain.
